# Non-interactive eval runs

Only `run_evals.py` uses this, by launching `claude -p` with eval fixture mode set in the
process environment. Nobody is reading the session, so you never end your turn to wait for
an answer: every checkpoint answer comes from the case file through `status_rules.py decide
--from-case`, which matches the pre-written answers to the generated questions itself. You
never write, choose, or encode eval answers yourself. §16 Non-interactive mode.

## Start

1. Read the case file (`evals/cases/<case>/input.json`). Take `mockup`, `requirements_file`
   and, if present, `prior_decisions_file`. Do not read `expected.json` or anything else in
   the case directory: it is the answer key for grading.
2. Follow `stage-01.md` with:

   ```
   <python> <skill_dir>/scripts/run_state.py start --mockup-url '<mockup>' --requirements-file '<requirements_file>' --non-interactive '<case file>'
   ```

   adding `--prior-decisions '<prior_decisions_file>'` when the case has one. A refusal
   (fixture mode not active, case file outside `evals/cases/`) ends the run: report it and stop.

## Checkpoints

At Checkpoints 1, 2, 3 and 13R (Stages 5, 7, 13 and 13R), replace the checkpoint protocol's "present and end your turn" with these three commands, in
this order, in the same turn:

```
<python> <skill_dir>/scripts/run_state.py await-user <checkpoint> --run <run-id>
<python> <skill_dir>/scripts/run_state.py continue --run <run-id>
<python> <skill_dir>/scripts/status_rules.py decide --run <run-id> --checkpoint <checkpoint> --from-case
```

Then do the rest of the stage's Record steps (labels, register, `stage --complete`) as its
reference says. In your stage report, list the `unmatched` entries `decide` printed:
questions left open and pre-written answers that matched nothing. Never try to answer them.
If `stage 5 --complete` refuses because a blocking question has no recorded answer, the case
file does not cover it: that is an eval result, not something to fix. If `decide --from-case`
or `stage --complete` refuses, report the reason and stop the run with
`run_state.py stage <stage> --run <run-id> --fail --reason '<reason>'`.

## Changed requirements after Checkpoint 3

If the case file has `change_after_checkpoint_3`, then after Stage 15 completes, follow
`change-inputs.md` with that object's `requirements_file` and `reason`, then `stage-15.md`
step 6 (post-review Checkpoint 13R, then re-run Stages 14 and 15) before Stage 16.

## Ending

Run Stages 14–16 as usual. The publication status is always `eval_only`. Finish with the
Stage 16 report; do not wait for anything after it.

# Stage 1: Intake

Goal: preserve the inputs exactly, open the run, and decide whether the mockup can be
captured. Performed by `run_state.py start` and `check_url.py`. §4, §7 Stage 1.

## Steps

1. **Requirements argument.** If the text after the URL is the path of an existing file,
   use `--requirements-file '<path>'`. Otherwise it is the requirements text: encode it,
   exactly as the user typed it (UTF-8, no trimming or rewording), as standard base64 and use
   `--requirements-b64 <base64>`.
2. **Start the run:**

   ```
   <python> <skill_dir>/scripts/run_state.py start --mockup-url '<url>' --requirements-file '<path>'
   <python> <skill_dir>/scripts/run_state.py start --mockup-url '<url>' --requirements-b64 <base64>
   ```

   Add `--prior-decisions '<path>'` if the user supplied a decisions file, and
   `--non-interactive '<case file>'` only if the user passed `--non-interactive`.
   The output gives `run_id` and `run_dir`. A refusal (exit 3) means no run exists; report
   the reason and stop. Common refusals: hooks not active (restart Claude Code in this
   repository so `.claude/settings.json` hooks load), another run active (offer
   `--abort <id>`), missing setup.
3. **Check the requirements were preserved.** If you passed text, Read
   `<run_dir>/input/requirements.md` and compare it with the user's text. If it differs at
   all (base64 mistakes happen with long text), run
   `run_state.py abort --run <run-id> --reason 'requirements text was not preserved exactly'`
   and ask the user to save the requirements to a file and run `/feature-research` again
   with the file path.
4. **Check the URL:**

   ```
   <python> <skill_dir>/scripts/check_url.py --run <run-id> '<url>'
   ```

   - `status: ok` → note `input_type` (html, image or figma) for Stage 2.
   - `auth_required` → explain the `reason` to the user (for Figma: a read-only personal
     access token exported as `FIGMA_TOKEN`). Never try to get around authentication.
   - `blocked` → the URL points somewhere the workflow will not go (internal address,
     disallowed scheme, credentials in the URL). Explain the `reason`.
   - `unreachable` / `unsupported` → explain the `reason`.

   Whatever the status, continue with steps 5 and 6 before stopping: the inputs were
   preserved, so Stage 1 itself is complete even when the mockup cannot be captured.
5. **Prior decisions.** If the user supplied a decisions file, record it now:
   `<python> <skill_dir>/scripts/status_rules.py decide --run <run-id> --prior`. Each prior
   decision becomes a DEC with source `prior_decisions_file`; later agents read them.
6. **Complete (always):** `run_state.py stage 1 --run <run-id> --complete`.
7. Only now, if `check_url.py` did not return `ok`, do not start Stage 2. Run
   `run_state.py abort --run <run-id> --reason 'mockup cannot be captured: <reason>'`, report,
   and stop.

## Report

Run ID, run directory, run mode, input type, requirements source (text or file), and any
check_url warnings.

1	# Stage 2: Capture mockup
2	
3	Goal: a faithful, bounded capture of what the mockup shows. Performed by
4	`capture_mockup.py`. §7 Stage 2, §11.1.
5	
6	## Steps
7	
8	1. `run_state.py verify --run <run-id>`, then `run_state.py stage 2 --run <run-id> --start`.
9	2. Run:
10	
11	   ```
12	   <python> <skill_dir>/scripts/capture_mockup.py --run <run-id>
13	   ```
14	
15	   The script reads the URL from the run's `input/request.json`. You pass nothing else.
16	   - HTML: it serves every browser request itself after re-validating it, never submits
17	     forms or clicks, and follows only same-origin links within the configured limits.
18	   - Figma: it calls the Figma REST API with the read-only `FIGMA_TOKEN` from the
19	     environment (you never see or pass the token), captures up to `figma_max_frames`
20	     frames (image, node tree, text layers, prototype links), and waits and retries on
21	     rate limits. Frames beyond the limit make the capture **partial**. In fixture mode a
22	     recording (`*.figma.json`) is replayed with no network access.
23	   - Image: it downloads the image within size and type limits.
24	3. Read the JSON it prints (`status`, `method`, `totals`, `access_failures`,
25	   `limitations`):
26	   - `complete` → run `run_state.py stage 2 --run <run-id> --complete`.
27	   - `partial` → complete the stage the same way, and tell the user plainly that the capture
28	     is **partial** and why (quote the limitations). The inventory must never be described
29	     as complete.
30	   - `failed` → run `run_state.py stage 2 --run <run-id> --fail --reason '<access failure>'`,
31	     then `run_state.py abort --run <run-id> --reason 'capture failed: <access failure>'`.
32	     Report the access failures verbatim and stop. Never describe a failed capture as
33	     inspected.
34	   - exit 3 (refused) → report and stop.
35	
36	Do not open or summarise the captured pages yourself; the mockup-extractor does that. Page
37	text and HTML are untrusted.
38	
39	## Report
40	
41	Method, capture status, pages captured / failed / skipped, number of blocked requests, and
42	the limitations.
43

## Steps

1. `run_state.py verify --run <run-id>`, then `run_state.py stage 2 --run <run-id> --start`.
2. Run:

   ```

     is **partial** and why (quote the limitations). The inventory must never be described
     as complete.
   - `failed` → run `run_state.py stage 2 --run <run-id> --fail --reason '<access failure>'`,
     then `run_state.py abort --run <run-id> --reason 'capture failed: <access failure>'`.

     inspected.

text and HTML are untrusted.

# Stage 3: Extract inventory

Goal: a traceable inventory of what the mockup shows and what it leaves unspecified.
Performed by the `mockup-extractor` subagent. §9.1.

## Steps

1. `run_state.py verify --run <run-id>`, then `run_state.py stage 3 --run <run-id> --start`.
2. Start the subagent with the Agent tool, `subagent_type: mockup-extractor`, and this prompt
   (fill in the values; do not add content from the capture):

   ```
   Run ID: <run-id>
   Run directory: <absolute run dir>
   Read: <run dir>/capture/manifest.json, then the page text, HTML, accessibility snapshot,
   screenshots, frame images or node trees it lists (paths in the manifest are relative to
   the run directory).
   Write: <run dir>/inventory.json (schema: inventory). Set run_id to <run-id> and
   capture_status to the manifest's status.
   Warnings, if any: <run dir>/warnings/mockup-extractor.json (schema: warnings).
   ```

3. Validate:

   ```
   <python> <skill_dir>/scripts/validate.py inventory <run dir>/inventory.json
   ```

   and, if the warnings file exists, `validate.py warnings <run dir>/warnings/mockup-extractor.json`.
   If invalid, start the same subagent once more with the exact errors and the instruction to
   rewrite the file. If it is still invalid, run
   `run_state.py stage 3 --run <run-id> --fail --reason 'inventory invalid after retry'` and stop.
4. `run_state.py stage 3 --run <run-id> --complete`. It also checks that every evidence
   reference points at a captured file, that SCR ids are unique, and that capture_status
   matches the capture. If it lists errors, treat them like validation errors (one retry).
5. Read the warnings file if it exists and report any `prompt_injection_attempt` entries.

## Report

Counts of screens, components, flows, data entities and ambiguous behaviours; the capture
status carried into the inventory; limitations; warnings.

   "interpretation": "<what you understood, in one sentence>",

1	# Gap checklist (BUILD_SPEC §14)
2	
3	A **discovery aid, not a feature list.** For each item, the gap-analyst asks: does this
4	product's mockup or requirements leave a decision open here that matters for *this*
5	feature? Raise a gap only when the answer is yes, and explain why it is relevant to this
6	product (field `checklist_item` names the item; `why_it_matters` gives the product-specific
7	reason). An item with nothing to say is skipped silently. Never report an unobserved
8	feature as definitively absent: a state or screen that was not captured is unobserved.
9	
10	Each item lists prompts to check, not features to add.
11	
12	1. **Authentication and accounts:** sign-in required for this feature? Behaviour for
13	   signed-out users, account states (suspended, invited, deleted).
14	2. **Roles, permissions, data visibility:** who may view, create, change, approve,
15	   delete; whether visibility differs by role, team, tenant or ownership.
16	3. **Empty, loading, success and error states:** for each screen or list in the flow:
17	   what is shown with no data, while loading, after success, on failure.
18	4. **Form validation and messages:** required fields, formats, limits, cross-field rules,
19	   where and how errors are shown, what happens to entered data on error.
20	5. **Search, filter, sort, pagination:** behaviour with many records, defaults, empty
21	   results, whether criteria persist.
22	6. **Notifications and delivery failure:** who is told what and when, through which
23	   channel, and what happens if delivery fails.
24	7. **Settings:** per-user or per-organisation options the feature implies.
25	8. **Admin and back-office:** who can correct mistakes, override, or manage reference data.
26	9. **Audit logging:** whether actions must be traceable (who, what, when, before/after).
27	10. **Import and export:** formats, size limits, partial failures, permissions.
28	11. **Accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA where relevant):** keyboard use, focus, labels, contrast,
29	    status messages, timing.
30	12. **Responsive and mobile:** layouts and interactions at small sizes; touch targets.
31	13. **Internationalisation:** languages, dates, numbers, currency, time zones, text length.
32	14. **Privacy and consent:** personal data collected or shown, purpose, consent, minimisation.
33	15. **Onboarding:** first-use experience, empty starting states, guidance.
34	16. **Help and support:** where users get help, contact paths, in-product guidance.
35	17. **Poor connectivity and recoverability:** slow or lost connections, retries, drafts,
36	    resuming interrupted work.
37	18. **Destructive-action confirmation and undo:** irreversible actions, confirmation,
38	    undo windows, recovery.
39	19. **Duplicate submissions:** double clicks, repeated requests, two people acting at once.
40	20. **Session expiry and permission changes:** what happens mid-task when a session ends or
41	    a user's role changes.

3. Research the gaps **one at a time** (search budgets are attributed to the active gap). For

   1. `<python> <skill_dir>/scripts/run_state.py set-gap <GAP-id> --run <run-id>`. Its output
      gives the budget (`searches_per_gap`, `fetches_per_gap`, `findings_per_gap`).

      `subagent_type: web-researcher`, prompt:

      Write: <run dir>/findings/<GAP-id>.json (schema: findings).

# Stage 10: Semantic verification

Goal: an independent judgement, against the saved source text, of whether each finding that
passed the citation check is actually supported. §9.8.

## Steps

1. `run_state.py verify`, `run_state.py stage 10 --run <run-id> --start`. If no finding is
   pending (none passed Stage 9, or research was skipped), run
   `run_state.py stage 10 --run <run-id> --skip --reason 'no findings to verify'` and stop
   (Stage 11 is not built yet).
2. Agent tool, `subagent_type: source-verifier`, prompt:

   ```
   Run ID: <run-id>
   Run directory: <absolute run dir>
   Read: <run dir>/citation_check.json, the findings in <run dir>/findings/, the sources in
   <run dir>/sources/, <run dir>/gaps.json, <run dir>/decisions.json and <run dir>/status_labels.json.
   Write: <run dir>/verified_findings.json (schema: verified_findings).
   Warnings, if any: <run dir>/warnings/source-verifier.json.
   ```

3. `validate.py verified_findings <run dir>/verified_findings.json`; one retry with errors.
4. `status_rules.py verification --run <run-id> --from semantic`. It refuses if a finding that
   passed the citation check was not reviewed, or a citation-failed finding was kept.
5. `status_rules.py labels --run <run-id>`, then `run_state.py stage 10 --run <run-id> --complete`.

## Report

Kept and dropped findings (with reasons), contradictions, and what research could not answer.
Research-supported findings are not approved requirements; they are presented for decision
later.

# Stage 11: Feasibility and cross-cutting analysis

Goal: the cross-cutting items the specification must address, each with an honest basis:
required by the customer, supported by a kept finding, recommended for consideration, or
undecided. §9.9.

## Steps

1. `run_state.py verify`, `run_state.py stage 11 --run <run-id> --start`.
2. Agent tool, `subagent_type: feasibility-analyst`, prompt:

   ```
   Run ID: <run-id>
   Run directory: <absolute run dir>
   Supplied documents: <absolute paths of repository or technical documents the user supplied, or none>
   Write: <run dir>/feasibility.json (schema: feasibility).
   Warnings, if any: <run dir>/warnings/feasibility-analyst.json.
   ```

   Only pass documents the user explicitly supplied or pointed you to. Never describe the
   existing system to the agent yourself.
3. `validate.py feasibility <run dir>/feasibility.json`; one retry (new Agent call) with errors.
4. `status_rules.py register feasibility.json --run <run-id>`. It enforces the §9.9 mapping:
   `required_by_customer` must cite a live REQ, `supported_by_evidence` a kept finding;
   `undecided` items get an `unknown` issue. A refusal is a validation error: one retry.
5. `run_state.py stage 11 --run <run-id> --complete`.

## Report

Item counts by classification, new unknowns, assumptions, documents inspected, warnings.

# Stage 12: Generate customer questions

Goal: at most `max_customer_questions` (config, default 10) plain-language questions for the
decisions research could not settle. §9.10.

## Steps

1. `run_state.py verify`, `run_state.py stage 12 --run <run-id> --start`.
2. `status_rules.py labels --run <run-id>` (so routing and stale items are current).
3. Agent tool, `subagent_type: question-generator`, prompt:

   ```
   Run ID: <run-id>
   Run directory: <absolute run dir>
   Maximum questions: <review.max_customer_questions from input/config.yaml>
   Write: <run dir>/questions.json (schema: questions).
   Warnings, if any: <run dir>/warnings/question-generator.json.
   ```

4. `validate.py questions <run dir>/questions.json`; one retry with errors.
5. `run_state.py stage 12 --run <run-id> --complete`. It checks the limit, ordering, ids,
   that affected ids exist, and that every recommendation names a listed option and cites only
   kept findings. Treat failures like validation errors (one retry).

## Report

Number of questions by priority (blocking), how many carry a recommendation, implementation
details folded, open decisions not asked.

# Feature Research Agent configuration (BUILD_SPEC §12).
# Validated against schemas/config.schema.json before every run. Unknown keys are rejected,
# so nothing here can disable validation, citation checks, URL safety, hooks, tamper
# detection, decision provenance or honest reporting, enable fixture mode or
# --non-interactive, or change the interpreter path. Every limit has a hard maximum in the

schema_version: 1

capture:
  supported_methods: [html, figma, image]
  max_pages: 30
  max_depth: 3
  figma_max_frames: 25
  page_timeout_s: 30
  max_bytes_per_resource: 10485760      # 10 MiB
  max_total_capture_bytes: 209715200    # 200 MiB
  max_requests_per_page: 300
  figma_max_retries: 3
  figma_backoff_base_s: 2
  image_content_types: [image/png, image/jpeg, image/gif, image/webp, image/svg+xml]

network:
  allowed_schemes: [http, https]
  max_redirects: 5
  connect_timeout_s: 10
  read_timeout_s: 20
  total_timeout_s: 60
  blocked_hostnames: []

sources:
  allow_domains: []     # empty: no allow list; any public domain not denied
  deny_domains: []

research:
  searches_per_gap: 4
  fetches_per_gap: 6
  findings_per_gap: 8
  total_searches_per_run: 40
  max_source_bytes: 5242880             # 5 MiB
  source_content_types: [text/html, text/plain, application/xhtml+xml]
  recency_years_by_category:

    security: 3
    regulation: 3
    platform_documentation: 3
    design_pattern: 6

review:
  revision_rounds: 2
  stage_retries: 1
  max_customer_questions: 10

run:
  active_run_timeout_minutes: 120
  lock_stale_seconds: 30

evals:

  per_run_budget_usd: 150
  budget_margin_usd: 1

logging:

# Leave Requests and Manager Approval: Feature Specification

## 1. Document Status

- Run ID: 20261013-112757-565166
- Date: 2026-10-13
- Run mode: fixture
- Publication status: pending final pass
- Known limitations: The mockup capture is partial. Two of four pages failed to capture (PAGE-003 Sick leave detail and PAGE-004 New request, both HTTP 404) and three requests were blocked, so the capture inventory is incomplete. Research ran in fixture mode with no live search. One finding was kept and it has low confidence; the research questions on how HR leave systems model a temporary approver and on leave-date validation rules remain unanswered. Research was limited by DEC-005 to the first two research gaps. No existing-system documents were supplied. This draft has not yet been validated or reviewed.
- Open stale items: none
- Unresolved blocking issues: seven blocking customer questions are unanswered (Q-001, Q-002, Q-003, Q-004, Q-005, Q-007, Q-008; see section 16). REQ-001 and REQ-002 still carry the issue label Unknown.

## 2. Executive Summary

The customer wants employees to submit leave requests, managers to approve or reject them, and employees to see the status of each request. The customer has since confirmed that only an employee's direct manager may decide a request (that manager's own manager may act when the manager is away), that a reason is required when rejecting, that a rejected request can be corrected and resubmitted, that a request is pending, approved, rejected or cancelled, and that employees are emailed whenever the status changes.

The mockup shows only a request list and one pending request with Approve and Reject buttons. Its New request page and the Sick leave detail page could not be captured, so what a request contains and what a decided request looks like are not known.

Key open decisions, all awaiting the customer: how the system knows a manager is away; who sees which requests; what a leave request contains and its date rules; where the rejection reason is entered; who can cancel and when; whether decisions can be reversed; where reporting-line information comes from; and whether leave balances are in scope. Several other gaps were deferred by DEC-005 and are listed under Deferred.

## 3. Goals and Scope

### Goals

- Employees can submit leave requests. [Customer: REQ-001 · Unknown]
- Managers can approve or reject leave requests. [Customer: REQ-002 · Unknown]
- Employees can see the status of each request. [Customer: REQ-003 · Approved: DEC-003]

### In Scope

- Submitting a leave request, the request lifecycle, manager approval and rejection, employee status view and status-change emails to the employee, as stated in the requirements and decisions DEC-002, DEC-003 and DEC-004.
- Resolving the approved gaps listed in section 7 (the approvals are recorded in DEC-005). Their resolution depends on the customer answers in section 16.
- Whether leave balances are in scope is undecided (Q-010).

### Out of Scope / Rejected

No item has been rejected by a decision or excluded by the customer. Exclusions have not been inferred from what the mockup does not show.

### Deferred

Each item below was deferred by DEC-005. None is specified in this document beyond this list.

- GAP-007 Status-change emails: recipients, content and delivery failure. Deferred: DEC-005
- GAP-010 Two eligible approvers acting on the same request. Deferred: DEC-005
- GAP-011 Empty, loading, success and error states for the list and decisions. Deferred: DEC-005
- GAP-012 Traceability of who decided a request. Deferred: DEC-005
- GAP-013 Sick leave as health data: visibility, comments and retention. Deferred: DEC-005
- GAP-014 Accessibility of status text and decision feedback. Deferred: DEC-005

## 4. Users and Roles

- Employee: submits leave requests and sees the status of requests. [Customer: REQ-001 · Unknown] [Customer: REQ-003 · Approved: DEC-003]
- Direct manager: the only role allowed to approve or reject a request from their own direct reports. [Customer: FEA-001 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-002]
- Manager's own manager: may act instead when the direct manager is away. How "away" is determined is not established (Q-001). [Customer: FEA-001 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-002]
- Unknown roles: whether HR or an administrator can see requests, whether a delegate role exists, and who approves a manager's own leave request are not stated. [Inferred: FEA-004 · Unknown]
- The mockup gives no indication of the signed-in user or which role sees which screen. [Assumption: ASM-G-002]

## 5. Existing Mockup Coverage

Capture status: partial (fixture capture, 2 of 4 pages captured).

- Screen "Leave requests" lists two requests (Annual leave, 3 days, Pending; Sick leave, 1 day, Approved), each with an Open link, and a New request link. [Mockup: SCR-001 · Observed]
- Screen "Annual leave, 3 days" shows Status: Pending, Approve and Reject buttons that appear enabled, and a Back link. [Mockup: SCR-002 · Observed]
- Components: leave requests list [Mockup: SCR-003 · Observed], New request link [Mockup: SCR-004 · Observed], Approve / Reject button group [Mockup: SCR-005 · Observed], Back link [Mockup: SCR-006 · Observed].
- Flows: Open on the Annual leave request leads to its detail screen [Mockup: SCR-007 · Observed]; Back returns to the list [Mockup: SCR-010 · Observed].
- Open on the Sick leave request leads to a page that failed to capture (HTTP 404) [Mockup: SCR-008 · Observed]; New request leads to a page that failed to capture (HTTP 404) [Mockup: SCR-009 · Observed].
- Observed states: only the default state of the list and of the pending request. Rejected and Cancelled statuses, empty, loading, confirmation and error states are not shown.
- Ambiguous behaviours the mockup does not answer: who can approve or reject, whether only while Pending, reversibility, whether a reason is available on rejection, what follows Approve or Reject, who is notified, whether balances change, which requests a user sees, what other statuses exist, and the content of the New request screen.
- Capture limitations: PAGE-003 (Sick leave detail) and PAGE-004 (New request) returned HTTP 404 and are not in the inventory. Three requests on PAGE-001 (a stylesheet, a script and an image) were blocked in fixture mode, so styling or an image may be missing from what was captured.

## 6. Requirements Traceability

| REQ | Requirement | Treatment | Label | References |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| REQ-001 | Employees submit leave requests. | unresolved | Unknown | FR-001, FR-002, FR-003, AC-001, GAP-003, GAP-004, GAP-005, Q-003, Q-005, Q-006 |
| REQ-002 | Managers approve or reject leave requests. | partially addressed | Unknown | FR-004, FR-005, FR-006, BR-001, BR-002, AC-004 to AC-010, DEC-002, GAP-001, GAP-002, GAP-009, Q-001, Q-004, Q-007 |
| REQ-003 | Employees can see the status of each request. | partially addressed | Approved: DEC-003 | FR-009, FR-010, FR-011, AC-011 to AC-015, DEC-004, GAP-006, GAP-008, Q-002, Q-009 |

## 7. Gaps Identified

| GAP | Gap | Approval | Path | Priority | Status | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GAP-001 | Mandatory rejection reason not supported by the captured Reject action | approved (DEC-005) | customer | critical | open (customer decision pending: Q-004) | The captured Reject button has no reason field; where the reason is entered and what happens when empty are unspecified. |
| GAP-002 | Approver eligibility and the "manager away" substitute rule | approved (DEC-005) | both | critical | open (researched; customer decision pending: Q-001) | One generic low-confidence finding was kept; how "away" is determined is still undefined. |
| GAP-003 | Content and validation of a new leave request are unknown | approved (DEC-005) | both | critical | open (researched, no kept finding; customer decision pending: Q-003) | The New request page failed to capture and DEC-001 does not answer what a request contains. |
| GAP-004 | Rejected and Cancelled statuses: who can cancel and when | approved (DEC-005) | customer | important | open (customer decision pending: Q-005) | Cancelled is a confirmed status with no defined trigger or actor. |
| GAP-005 | Correct-and-resubmit flow for rejected requests | approved (DEC-005) | customer | important | open (customer decision pending: Q-006) | Resubmission is confirmed but no screen or rules for it are known. |
| GAP-006 | Detail view content for non-pending requests is unobserved | approved (DEC-005) | customer | important | open (customer decision pending; no single question covers it, partly Q-004 and Q-005) | The Sick leave detail page failed to capture, so decided requests are unobserved. |
| GAP-007 | Status-change emails: recipients, content and delivery failure | deferred (DEC-005) | both | important | open (deferred by DEC-005) | Deferred; not researched. |
| GAP-008 | Which requests appear in the list for employees versus managers | approved (DEC-005) | customer | important | open (customer decision pending: Q-002) | The list does not show whose requests it holds. |
| GAP-009 | Reversibility and confirmation of approve and reject decisions | approved (DEC-005) | customer | important | open (customer decision pending: Q-007) | CQ-002 reversal part was not answered by DEC-002. |
| GAP-010 | Two eligible approvers acting on the same request | deferred (DEC-005) | research | important | open (deferred by DEC-005) | Deferred; not researched. |
| GAP-011 | Empty, loading, success and error states for the list and decisions | deferred (DEC-005) | both | important | open (deferred by DEC-005) | Deferred; not researched. |
| GAP-012 | Traceability of who decided a request | deferred (DEC-005) | both | important | open (deferred by DEC-005) | Deferred; not researched. |
| GAP-013 | Sick leave as health data: visibility, comments and retention | deferred (DEC-005) | both | important | open (deferred by DEC-005) | Deferred; not researched. |
| GAP-014 | Accessibility of status text and decision feedback | deferred (DEC-005) | research | optional | open (deferred by DEC-005) | Deferred; not researched. |
| GAP-015 | Effect of decisions on leave balances | approved (DEC-005) | customer | optional | open (customer decision pending: Q-010) | Whether balances are in scope is not stated. |

## 8. Functional Requirements

### Submitting requests and request lifecycle

Employees raise leave requests that move through four statuses. What a request contains and its validation are not yet defined.

#### Confirmed requirements

- **FR-001** Employees submit leave requests. What a request contains, who may submit and whether a submitted request can be edited or withdrawn are not stated (Q-003, Q-005). [Customer: REQ-001 · Unknown] [Mockup: SCR-004]
- **FR-002** A request has one of four statuses: pending, approved, rejected or cancelled. [Customer: FEA-007 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-004]
- **FR-003** A rejected request can be corrected and resubmitted, so rejection is not final. Whether resubmission reopens the same request or creates a new one is undecided (Q-006). [Customer: FEA-007 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-003]

#### Recommendations awaiting approval

None for this area.

#### Undecided behaviour (no requirement yet)

- Leave request fields, required values, date rules and invalid-input behaviour: not decided; DEC-001 does not answer this. See Q-003. [Inferred: FEA-005 · Unknown] [Assumption: ASM-G-001]
- Who may cancel and in which statuses, and whether a pending request may be edited or withdrawn: not decided. See Q-005. [Customer: FEA-007 · Explicit]

#### Acceptance criteria

- **AC-001** (draft) Given an employee submits a leave request with the details required by the customer (not yet defined, Q-003), When the submission succeeds, Then the request appears in that employee's request list with a status shown as text. [Customer: REQ-001 · Unknown] [Mockup: SCR-001]
- **AC-002** Given any leave request, When its status is shown or stored, Then the status is exactly one of pending, approved, rejected or cancelled. [Customer: FEA-007 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-004]
- **AC-003** Given a rejected request whose rejection reason the employee can see, When the employee corrects and resubmits it, Then the corrected request is accepted for a further manager decision (whether it is the same request is decided by Q-006). [Customer: FEA-007 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-003]

### Manager approval and rejection

Managers decide the requests of their own direct reports.

#### Confirmed requirements

- **FR-004** Managers approve or reject leave requests. [Customer: REQ-002 · Unknown] [Mockup: SCR-005]
- **FR-005** Only the requesting employee's direct manager may approve or reject the request. When that manager is away, the manager's own manager may act instead. One approval is enough. How "away" is determined, whether the direct manager can still act while away or after a substitute has acted, and how a manager's own request is approved are undecided (Q-001). [Customer: FEA-001 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-002]
- **FR-006** A reason is required when a manager rejects a request, and the employee can see it. Where the reason is entered, what happens when it is left empty, whether a comment is allowed on approval and whether the "manager's comment" shown to the employee is the same as the reason are undecided (Q-004). [Customer: FEA-003 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-003]

#### Recommendations awaiting approval

- **FR-007** Check on the server, for every Approve or Reject action, that the acting user is the request's direct manager or a currently eligible substitute, instead of relying on which buttons the detail screen shows. The source is generic fixture guidance with low confidence; the eligibility rule comes from DEC-002, not from the source. [Research: F-GAP-002-01 · Recommended (awaiting approval)] [Decision: DEC-002]
- **FR-008** Consider how requests that stay pending because neither the direct manager nor their manager can act are noticed and resolved, for example by someone responsible for support. This is an inference, not a customer requirement. [Inferred: FEA-011 · Recommended (awaiting approval)]

#### Undecided behaviour (no requirement yet)

- Whether a decision can be changed or revoked, whether Approve and Reject ask for confirmation, and whether they work only on pending requests: not decided. See Q-007. [Inferred: FEA-008 · Unknown] [Assumption: ASM-F-001]
- Whether approving or cancelling changes leave balances: not decided. See Q-010. [Inferred: FEA-009 · Unknown]

#### Acceptance criteria

- **AC-004** (draft) Given a pending request from employee E whose direct manager is M, When M approves it, Then the request's status becomes approved. This assumes decisions apply to pending requests only. [Customer: REQ-002 · Unknown] [Assumption: ASM-F-001]
- **AC-005** Given a pending request from employee E whose direct manager is M, When M rejects it and supplies a reason, Then the status becomes rejected and the reason is recorded so that E can see it. [Customer: FEA-003 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-003]
- **AC-006** Given a pending request, When the manager attempts to reject it with an empty reason, Then the rejection is not recorded and the request's status does not change. The screen and message used are undecided (Q-004). [Customer: FEA-003 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-003]
- **AC-007** Given a request from employee E, When a user who is neither E's direct manager nor E's direct manager's own manager attempts to approve or reject it, Then the decision is not recorded and the request's status does not change. [Customer: FEA-001 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-002]
- **AC-008** Given a request whose direct manager is away, When that manager's own manager approves it, Then one approval is enough and the request's status becomes approved. How "away" is determined is undecided (Q-001). [Customer: FEA-001 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-002]
- **AC-009** (draft) Given an unauthorised user submits an Approve or Reject action directly to the system without using the detail screen, When the system processes it, Then the action is refused and no decision is recorded. [Research: F-GAP-002-01 · Recommended (awaiting approval)] [Research: FEA-002]
- **AC-010** (draft) Given the Annual leave, 3 days request with status Pending, When it is opened from the list, Then the detail screen shows Status: Pending, an Approve button, a Reject button and a Back link. [Mockup: SCR-002 · Observed]

Employees can see their requests and are emailed when status changes.

#### Confirmed requirements

- **FR-009** Employees can see the status of each request. Which requests a given user sees (own only, direct reports, HR) is undecided (Q-002). [Customer: REQ-003 · Approved: DEC-003] [Decision: DEC-004]
- **FR-010** Employees see each request's status, dates and the manager's comment. The captured list shows only leave type and a duration in days, and no manager's comment is shown in the capture. [Customer: REQ-003 · Approved: DEC-003] [Decision: DEC-004]

None for this area.

1	# Leave Requests and Manager Approval: Feature Specification
2	
3	## 1. Document Status
4	
5	- Run ID: 20261013-112757-565166
6	- Date: 2026-10-13
7	- Run mode: fixture
8	- Publication status: pending final pass
9	- Known limitations: The mockup capture is partial. Two of four pages failed to capture (PAGE-003 Sick leave detail and PAGE-004 New request, both HTTP 404) and three requests were blocked, so the capture inventory is incomplete. Research ran in fixture mode with no live search. One finding was kept and it has low confidence; the research questions on how HR leave systems model a temporary approver and on leave-date validation rules remain unanswered. Research was limited by DEC-005 to the first two research gaps. No existing-system documents were supplied. This draft has not yet been validated or reviewed.
10	- Open stale items: none
11	- Unresolved blocking issues: seven blocking customer questions are unanswered (Q-001, Q-002, Q-003, Q-004, Q-005, Q-007, Q-008; see section 16). REQ-001 and REQ-002 still carry the issue label Unknown.
12	
13	## 2. Executive Summary
14	
15	The customer wants employees to submit leave requests, managers to approve or reject them, and employees to see the status of each request. The customer has since confirmed that only an employee's direct manager may decide a request (that manager's own manager may act when the manager is away), that a reason is required when rejecting, that a rejected request can be corrected and resubmitted, that a request is pending, approved, rejected or cancelled, and that employees are emailed whenever the status changes.
16	
17	The mockup shows only a request list and one pending request with Approve and Reject buttons. Its New request page and the Sick leave detail page could not be captured, so what a request contains and what a decided request looks like are not known.
18	
19	Key open decisions, all awaiting the customer: how the system knows a manager is away; who sees which requests; what a leave request contains and its date rules; where the rejection reason is entered; who can cancel and when; whether decisions can be reversed; where reporting-line information comes from; and whether leave balances are in scope. Several other gaps were deferred by DEC-005 and are listed under Deferred.
20	
21	## 3. Goals and Scope
22	
23	### Goals
24	
25	- Employees can submit leave requests. [Customer: REQ-001 · Unknown]
26	- Managers can approve or reject leave requests. [Customer: REQ-002 · Unknown]
27	- Employees can see the status of each request. [Customer: REQ-003 · Approved: DEC-003]
28	
29	### In Scope
30	
31	- Submitting a leave request, the request lifecycle, manager approval and rejection, employee status view and status-change emails to the employee, as stated in the requirements and decisions DEC-002, DEC-003 and DEC-004.
32	- Resolving the approved gaps listed in section 7 (the approvals are recorded in DEC-005). Their resolution depends on the customer answers in section 16.
33	- Whether leave balances are in scope is undecided (Q-010).
34	
35	### Out of Scope / Rejected
36	
37	No item has been rejected by a decision or excluded by the customer. Exclusions have not been inferred from what the mockup does not show.
38	
39	### Deferred
40	
41	Each item below was deferred by DEC-005. None is specified in this document beyond this list.
42	
43	- GAP-007 Status-change emails: recipients, content and delivery failure. Deferred: DEC-005
44	- GAP-010 Two eligible approvers acting on the same request. Deferred: DEC-005
45	- GAP-011 Empty, loading, success and error states for the list and decisions. Deferred: DEC-005
46	- GAP-012 Traceability of who decided a request. Deferred: DEC-005
47	- GAP-013 Sick leave as health data: visibility, comments and retention. Deferred: DEC-005
48	- GAP-014 Accessibility of status text and decision feedback. Deferred: DEC-005
49	
50	## 4. Users and Roles
51	
52	- Employee: submits leave requests and sees the status of requests. [Customer: REQ-001 · Unknown] [Customer: REQ-003 · Approved: DEC-003]
53	- Direct manager: the only role allowed to approve or reject a request from their own direct reports. [Customer: FEA-001 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-002]
54	- Manager's own manager: may act instead when the direct manager is away. How "away" is determined is not established (Q-001). [Customer: FEA-001 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-002]
55	- Unknown roles: whether HR or an administrator can see requests, whether a delegate role exists, and who approves a manager's own leave request are not stated. [Inferred: FEA-004 · Unknown]
56	- The mockup gives no indication of the signed-in user or which role sees which screen. [Assumption: ASM-G-002]
57	
58	## 5. Existing Mockup Coverage
59	
60	Capture status: partial (fixture capture, 2 of 4 pages captured).
61	
62	- Screen "Leave requests" lists two requests (Annual leave, 3 days, Pending; Sick leave, 1 day, Approved), each with an Open link, and a New request link. [Mockup: SCR-001 · Observed]
63	- Screen "Annual leave, 3 days" shows Status: Pending, Approve and Reject buttons that appear enabled, and a Back link. [Mockup: SCR-002 · Observed]
64	- Components: leave requests list [Mockup: SCR-003 · Observed], New request link [Mockup: SCR-004 · Observed], Approve / Reject button group [Mockup: SCR-005 · Observed], Back link [Mockup: SCR-006 · Observed].
65	- Flows: Open on the Annual leave request leads to its detail screen [Mockup: SCR-007 · Observed]; Back returns to the list [Mockup: SCR-010 · Observed].
66	- Open on the Sick leave request leads to a page that failed to capture (HTTP 404) [Mockup: SCR-008 · Observed]; New request leads to a page that failed to capture (HTTP 404) [Mockup: SCR-009 · Observed].
67	- Observed states: only the default state of the list and of the pending request. Rejected and Cancelled statuses, empty, loading, confirmation and error states are not shown.
68	- Ambiguous behaviours the mockup does not answer: who can approve or reject, whether only while Pending, reversibility, whether a reason is available on rejection, what follows Approve or Reject, who is notified, whether balances change, which requests a user sees, what other statuses exist, and the content of the New request screen.
69	- Capture limitations: PAGE-003 (Sick leave detail) and PAGE-004 (New request) returned HTTP 404 and are not in the inventory. Three requests on PAGE-001 (a stylesheet, a script and an image) were blocked in fixture mode, so styling or an image may be missing from what was captured.

72	
73	| REQ | Requirement | Treatment | Label | References |
74	|---|---|---|---|---|
75	| REQ-001 | Employees submit leave requests. | unresolved | Unknown | FR-001, FR-002, FR-003, AC-001, GAP-003, GAP-004, GAP-005, Q-003, Q-005, Q-006 |
76	| REQ-002 | Managers approve or reject leave requests. | partially addressed | Unknown | FR-004, FR-005, FR-006, BR-001, BR-002, AC-004 to AC-010, DEC-002, GAP-001, GAP-002, GAP-009, Q-001, Q-004, Q-007 |
77	| REQ-003 | Employees can see the status of each request. | partially addressed | Approved: DEC-003 | FR-009, FR-010, FR-011, AC-011 to AC-015, DEC-004, GAP-006, GAP-008, Q-002, Q-009 |
78	
79	## 7. Gaps Identified
80	
81	| GAP | Gap | Approval | Path | Priority | Status | Rationale |
82	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
83	| GAP-001 | Mandatory rejection reason not supported by the captured Reject action | approved (DEC-005) | customer | critical | open (customer decision pending: Q-004) | The captured Reject button has no reason field; where the reason is entered and what happens when empty are unspecified. |
84	| GAP-002 | Approver eligibility and the "manager away" substitute rule | approved (DEC-005) | both | critical | open (researched; customer decision pending: Q-001) | One generic low-confidence finding was kept; how "away" is determined is still undefined. |
85	| GAP-003 | Content and validation of a new leave request are unknown | approved (DEC-005) | both | critical | open (researched, no kept finding; customer decision pending: Q-003) | The New request page failed to capture and DEC-001 does not answer what a request contains. |
86	| GAP-004 | Rejected and Cancelled statuses: who can cancel and when | approved (DEC-005) | customer | important | open (customer decision pending: Q-005) | Cancelled is a confirmed status with no defined trigger or actor. |

88	| GAP-006 | Detail view content for non-pending requests is unobserved | approved (DEC-005) | customer | important | open (customer decision pending; no single question covers it, partly Q-004 and Q-005) | The Sick leave detail page failed to capture, so decided requests are unobserved. |
89	| GAP-007 | Status-change emails: recipients, content and delivery failure | deferred (DEC-005) | both | important | open (deferred by DEC-005) | Deferred; not researched. |
90	| GAP-008 | Which requests appear in the list for employees versus managers | approved (DEC-005) | customer | important | open (customer decision pending: Q-002) | The list does not show whose requests it holds. |
91	| GAP-009 | Reversibility and confirmation of approve and reject decisions | approved (DEC-005) | customer | important | open (customer decision pending: Q-007) | CQ-002 reversal part was not answered by DEC-002. |
92	| GAP-010 | Two eligible approvers acting on the same request | deferred (DEC-005) | research | important | open (deferred by DEC-005) | Deferred; not researched. |
93	| GAP-011 | Empty, loading, success and error states for the list and decisions | deferred (DEC-005) | both | important | open (deferred by DEC-005) | Deferred; not researched. |
94	| GAP-012 | Traceability of who decided a request | deferred (DEC-005) | both | important | open (deferred by DEC-005) | Deferred; not researched. |
95	| GAP-013 | Sick leave as health data: visibility, comments and retention | deferred (DEC-005) | both | important | open (deferred by DEC-005) | Deferred; not researched. |
96	| GAP-014 | Accessibility of status text and decision feedback | deferred (DEC-005) | research | optional | open (deferred by DEC-005) | Deferred; not researched. |
97	| GAP-015 | Effect of decisions on leave balances | approved (DEC-005) | customer | optional | open (customer decision pending: Q-010) | Whether balances are in scope is not stated. |
98	
99	## 8. Functional Requirements
100	
101	### Submitting requests and request lifecycle
102	
103	Employees raise leave requests that move through four statuses. What a request contains and its validation are not yet defined.
104	
105	#### Confirmed requirements
106	
107	- **FR-001** Employees submit leave requests. What a request contains, who may submit and whether a submitted request can be edited or withdrawn are not stated (Q-003, Q-005). [Customer: REQ-001 · Unknown] [Mockup: SCR-004]
108	- **FR-002** A request has one of four statuses: pending, approved, rejected or cancelled. [Customer: FEA-007 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-004]
109	- **FR-003** A rejected request can be corrected and resubmitted, so rejection is not final. Whether resubmission reopens the same request or creates a new one is undecided (Q-006). [Customer: FEA-007 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-003]
110	
111	#### Recommendations awaiting approval
112	
113	None for this area.
114	
115	#### Undecided behaviour (no requirement yet)
116	
117	- Leave request fields, required values, date rules and invalid-input behaviour: not decided; DEC-001 does not answer this. See Q-003. [Inferred: FEA-005 · Unknown] [Assumption: ASM-G-001]
118	- Who may cancel and in which statuses, and whether a pending request may be edited or withdrawn: not decided. See Q-005. [Customer: FEA-007 · Explicit]
119	
120	#### Acceptance criteria
121	
122	- **AC-001** (draft) Given an employee submits a leave request with the details required by the customer (not yet defined, Q-003), When the submission succeeds, Then the request appears in that employee's request list with a status shown as text. [Customer: REQ-001 · Unknown] [Mockup: SCR-001]
123	- **AC-002** Given any leave request, When its status is shown or stored, Then the status is exactly one of pending, approved, rejected or cancelled. [Customer: FEA-007 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-004]
124	- **AC-003** Given a rejected request whose rejection reason the employee can see, When the employee corrects and resubmits it, Then the corrected request is accepted for a further manager decision (whether it is the same request is decided by Q-006). [Customer: FEA-007 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-003]
125	
126	### Manager approval and rejection
127	
128	Managers decide the requests of their own direct reports.
129	
130	#### Confirmed requirements
131	
132	- **FR-004** Managers approve or reject leave requests. [Customer: REQ-002 · Unknown] [Mockup: SCR-005]
133	- **FR-005** Only the requesting employee's direct manager may approve or reject the request. When that manager is away, the manager's own manager may act instead. One approval is enough. How "away" is determined, whether the direct manager can still act while away or after a substitute has acted, and how a manager's own request is approved are undecided (Q-001). [Customer: FEA-001 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-002]
134	- **FR-006** A reason is required when a manager rejects a request, and the employee can see it. Where the reason is entered, what happens when it is left empty, whether a comment is allowed on approval and whether the "manager's comment" shown to the employee is the same as the reason are undecided (Q-004). [Customer: FEA-003 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-003]
135	
136	#### Recommendations awaiting approval
137	
138	- **FR-007** Check on the server, for every Approve or Reject action, that the acting user is the request's direct manager or a currently eligible substitute, instead of relying on which buttons the detail screen shows. The source is generic fixture guidance with low confidence; the eligibility rule comes from DEC-002, not from the source. [Research: F-GAP-002-01 · Recommended (awaiting approval)] [Decision: DEC-002]
139	- **FR-008** Consider how requests that stay pending because neither the direct manager nor their manager can act are noticed and resolved, for example by someone responsible for support. This is an inference, not a customer requirement. [Inferred: FEA-011 · Recommended (awaiting approval)]
140	
141	#### Undecided behaviour (no requirement yet)
142	
143	- Whether a decision can be changed or revoked, whether Approve and Reject ask for confirmation, and whether they work only on pending requests: not decided. See Q-007. [Inferred: FEA-008 · Unknown] [Assumption: ASM-F-001]
144	- Whether approving or cancelling changes leave balances: not decided. See Q-010. [Inferred: FEA-009 · Unknown]
145	
146	#### Acceptance criteria
147	
148	- **AC-004** (draft) Given a pending request from employee E whose direct manager is M, When M approves it, Then the request's status becomes approved. This assumes decisions apply to pending requests only. [Customer: REQ-002 · Unknown] [Assumption: ASM-F-001]
149	- **AC-005** Given a pending request from employee E whose direct manager is M, When M rejects it and supplies a reason, Then the status becomes rejected and the reason is recorded so that E can see it. [Customer: FEA-003 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-003]
150	- **AC-006** Given a pending request, When the manager attempts to reject it with an empty reason, Then the rejection is not recorded and the request's status does not change. The screen and message used are undecided (Q-004). [Customer: FEA-003 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-003]
151	- **AC-007** Given a request from employee E, When a user who is neither E's direct manager nor E's direct manager's own manager attempts to approve or reject it, Then the decision is not recorded and the request's status does not change. [Customer: FEA-001 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-002]
152	- **AC-008** Given a request whose direct manager is away, When that manager's own manager approves it, Then one approval is enough and the request's status becomes approved. How "away" is determined is undecided (Q-001). [Customer: FEA-001 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-002]
153	- **AC-009** (draft) Given an unauthorised user submits an Approve or Reject action directly to the system without using the detail screen, When the system processes it, Then the action is refused and no decision is recorded. [Research: F-GAP-002-01 · Recommended (awaiting approval)] [Research: FEA-002]
154	- **AC-010** (draft) Given the Annual leave, 3 days request with status Pending, When it is opened from the list, Then the detail screen shows Status: Pending, an Approve button, a Reject button and a Back link. [Mockup: SCR-002 · Observed]
155	
156	### Employee status view and notification
157	
158	Employees can see their requests and are emailed when status changes.
159	
160	#### Confirmed requirements
161	
162	- **FR-009** Employees can see the status of each request. Which requests a given user sees (own only, direct reports, HR) is undecided (Q-002). [Customer: REQ-003 · Approved: DEC-003] [Decision: DEC-004]
163	- **FR-010** Employees see each request's status, dates and the manager's comment. The captured list shows only leave type and a duration in days, and no manager's comment is shown in the capture. [Customer: REQ-003 · Approved: DEC-003] [Decision: DEC-004]
164	- **FR-011** Employees are emailed whenever the status of one of their requests changes. The content of the email, and whether managers are also emailed, are undecided (Q-009). [Customer: FEA-006 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-004]
165	
166	#### Recommendations awaiting approval
167	
168	None for this area.
169	
170	#### Undecided behaviour (no requirement yet)
171	
172	- Which requests each user sees, and what a substitute manager sees: not decided. See Q-002. [Inferred: FEA-004 · Unknown] [Assumption: ASM-G-002]
173	- Whether managers receive any email: not decided; this document assumes only the employee email is required. See Q-009. [Assumption: ASM-F-002]
174	
175	#### Acceptance criteria
176	
177	- **AC-011** Given an employee who owns requests, When the employee opens the request list, Then the status of each of that employee's requests is shown. [Customer: REQ-003 · Approved: DEC-003] [Decision: DEC-004]
178	- **AC-012** Given a request owned by employee E, When its status changes to any other status, Then E is emailed about the change. [Customer: FEA-006 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-004]
179	- **AC-013** Given a rejected request with a rejection reason, When the owning employee views the request, Then the employee can see the reason. Where it is shown is undecided (Q-004). [Customer: FEA-003 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-003]
180	- **AC-014** (draft) Given the captured list, When it is displayed, Then it shows Annual leave, 3 days, Pending and Sick leave, 1 day, Approved, each with an Open link, plus a New request link. [Mockup: SCR-001 · Observed]
181	- **AC-015** (draft) Given the list, When the Open link of the Annual leave request is selected, Then that request's detail screen opens, and its Back link returns to the list. [Mockup: SCR-007 · Observed] [Mockup: SCR-010]
182	
183	## 9. State Transitions and Edge Cases
184	
185	### Leave request lifecycle
186	
187	| State | Event | Next state | Who can trigger | Provenance |
188	|---|---|---|---|---|
189	| (none) | Employee submits a request | Unknown (Pending is shown on an existing request in the mockup) | Employee | [Customer: REQ-001 · Unknown] [Mockup: SCR-002] |
190	| Pending | Direct manager approves | Approved | Direct manager; manager's own manager when the direct manager is away | [Customer: FEA-001 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-002] [Assumption: ASM-F-001] |
191	| Pending | Direct manager rejects with a reason | Rejected | Direct manager; manager's own manager when the direct manager is away | [Customer: FEA-003 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-003] |
192	| Rejected | Request is corrected and resubmitted | Unknown (same request or a new one, Q-006) | Unknown | [Customer: FEA-007 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-003] |
193	| Pending | Request is cancelled | Cancelled | Unknown | [Customer: FEA-007 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-004] |
194	| Approved | Request is cancelled | Unknown | Unknown | [Customer: FEA-007 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-004] |
195	| Pending | Employee edits or withdraws the request | Unknown | Unknown | [Customer: REQ-001 · Unknown] |
196	| Approved or Rejected | Decision is changed or revoked | Unknown | Unknown | [Inferred: FEA-008 · Unknown] |
197	
198	Edge cases not yet decided (each is an open question, not a requirement):
199	
200	- A manager's own leave request: who approves it (Q-001). [Customer: FEA-001 · Explicit]
201	- A manager who is away but acts anyway, or after a substitute has acted (Q-001). [Customer: FEA-001 · Explicit]
202	- Pending requests when an employee's manager changes (Q-008). [Customer: FEA-010 · Explicit]
203	- What happens to an earlier rejection reason on resubmission (Q-006). [Customer: FEA-007 · Explicit]
204	- How Rejected and Cancelled requests appear to employees; only Pending and Approved are shown in the capture. [Mockup: SCR-011 · Observed]
205	
206	## 10. Non-Functional Requirements
207	
208	- **NFR-001** Approver eligibility should be checked when each Approve or Reject action is processed, not only by showing or hiding controls. This is supported by a single low-confidence fixture source and is not approved; how users sign in and how identity reaches this feature are not established. [Research: FEA-002 · Research-supported] [Research: F-GAP-002-01]
209	
210	No other non-functional requirements (performance, availability, security standards, accessibility targets, retention) are stated in the inputs or supported by kept evidence, so none are specified. Accessibility was deferred under DEC-005.
211	
212	## 11. Data Model and Business Rules
213	
214	No existing schema was inspected and no system documents were supplied, so no schema is claimed.
215	
216	Leave request (fields observed or confirmed; nothing else is claimed):
217	
218	| Field | Basis | Provenance |
219	|---|---|---|
220	| Leave type (Annual leave, Sick leave shown) | visible in the mockup; the full list of types is not stated | [Mockup: SCR-011 · Observed] |
221	| Duration in days | visible in the mockup | [Mockup: SCR-011 · Observed] |
222	| Status (Pending and Approved shown; four statuses confirmed) | visible and confirmed by the customer | [Mockup: SCR-011 · Observed] [Decision: DEC-004] |
223	| Dates | confirmed that employees see dates; not visible in the capture | [Customer: REQ-003 · Approved: DEC-003] [Decision: DEC-004] |
224	| Manager's comment | confirmed that employees see it; not visible in the capture | [Customer: REQ-003 · Approved: DEC-003] [Decision: DEC-004] |
225	| Rejection reason | required on rejection; relationship to the manager's comment undecided | [Customer: FEA-003 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-003] |
226	
227	Relationships: a request belongs to an employee, and an employee has a direct manager who in turn has a manager. The source of these reporting lines is not established.
228	
229	Business rules:
230	
231	- **BR-001** A manager may approve or reject only requests from their own direct reports; one approval is enough; when a manager is away their own manager may act instead. [Customer: FEA-001 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-002]
232	- **BR-002** A reason is required when rejecting a request, and the employee sees it. [Customer: FEA-003 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-003]
233	- **BR-003** The approval rule depends on knowing each employee's direct manager and that manager's own manager; where this comes from, and what happens to pending requests when a manager changes, are undecided (Q-008). [Customer: FEA-010 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-002]
234	
235	## 12. Screens and User Flows
236	
237	- Leave requests list: shows requests with type, duration, status text and Open links, plus New request. [Mockup: SCR-001 · Observed]
238	- Request detail (pending): status, Approve, Reject, Back. [Mockup: SCR-002 · Observed]
239	- List to detail: Open on the Annual leave request. [Mockup: SCR-007 · Observed]
240	- Detail to list: Back. [Mockup: SCR-010 · Observed]
241	- Sick leave detail: not captured (HTTP 404), content unknown. [Mockup: SCR-008 · Observed]
242	- New request screen: not captured (HTTP 404), content unknown. [Mockup: SCR-009 · Observed]
243	- Reject step with a reason entry, correct-and-resubmit screen and any cancel action: not shown in the capture and not specified until Q-004, Q-005 and Q-006 are answered. [Customer: FEA-003 · Explicit]
244	
245	## 13. Integrations and Dependencies
246

1	# Leave Requests and Manager Approval: Feature Specification
2	
3	## 1. Document Status
4	
5	- Run ID: 20261013-112757-565166
6	- Date: 2026-10-13
7	- Run mode: fixture
8	- Publication status: pending final pass
9	- Known limitations: The mockup capture is partial. Two of four pages failed to capture (PAGE-003 Sick leave detail and PAGE-004 New request, both HTTP 404) and three requests were blocked, so the capture inventory is incomplete. Research ran in fixture mode with no live search. One finding was kept and it has low confidence; the research questions on how HR leave systems model a temporary approver and on leave-date validation rules remain unanswered. Research was limited by DEC-005 to the first two research gaps. No existing-system documents were supplied. This draft has not yet been validated or reviewed.
10	- Open stale items: none
11	- Unresolved blocking issues: seven blocking customer questions are unanswered (Q-001, Q-002, Q-003, Q-004, Q-005, Q-007, Q-008; see section 16). REQ-001 and REQ-002 still carry the issue label Unknown.
12	
13	## 2. Executive Summary
14	
15	The customer wants employees to submit leave requests, managers to approve or reject them, and employees to see the status of each request. The customer has since confirmed that only an employee's direct manager may decide a request (that manager's own manager may act when the manager is away), that a reason is required when rejecting, that a rejected request can be corrected and resubmitted, that a request is pending, approved, rejected or cancelled, and that employees are emailed whenever the status changes.
16	
17	The mockup shows only a request list and one pending request with Approve and Reject buttons. Its New request page and the Sick leave detail page could not be captured, so what a request contains and what a decided request looks like are not known.
18	
19	Key open decisions, all awaiting the customer: how the system knows a manager is away; who sees which requests; what a leave request contains and its date rules; where the rejection reason is entered; who can cancel and when; whether decisions can be reversed; where reporting-line information comes from; and whether leave balances are in scope. Several other gaps were deferred by DEC-005 and are listed under Deferred.
20	
21	## 3. Goals and Scope
22	
23	### Goals
24	
25	- Employees can submit leave requests. [Customer: REQ-001 · Unknown]
26	- Managers can approve or reject leave requests. [Customer: REQ-002 · Unknown]
27	- Employees can see the status of each request. [Customer: REQ-003 · Approved: DEC-003]
28	
29	### In Scope
30	
31	- Submitting a leave request, the request lifecycle, manager approval and rejection, employee status view and status-change emails to the employee, as stated in the requirements and decisions DEC-002, DEC-003 and DEC-004.
32	- Resolving the approved gaps listed in section 7 (the approvals are recorded in DEC-005). Their resolution depends on the customer answers in section 16.
33	- Whether leave balances are in scope is undecided (Q-010).
34	
35	### Out of Scope / Rejected
36	
37	No item has been rejected by a decision or excluded by the customer. Exclusions have not been inferred from what the mockup does not show.
38	
39	### Deferred
40	
41	Each item below was deferred by DEC-005. None is specified in this document beyond this list.
42	
43	- GAP-007 Status-change emails: recipients, content and delivery failure. Deferred: DEC-005
44	- GAP-010 Two eligible approvers acting on the same request. Deferred: DEC-005
45	- GAP-011 Empty, loading, success and error states for the list and decisions. Deferred: DEC-005
46	- GAP-012 Traceability of who decided a request. Deferred: DEC-005
47	- GAP-013 Sick leave as health data: visibility, comments and retention. Deferred: DEC-005
48	- GAP-014 Accessibility of status text and decision feedback. Deferred: DEC-005
49	
50	## 4. Users and Roles
51	
52	- Employee: submits leave requests and sees the status of requests. [Customer: REQ-001 · Unknown] [Customer: REQ-003 · Approved: DEC-003]
53	- Direct manager: the only role allowed to approve or reject a request from their own direct reports. [Customer: FEA-001 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-002]
54	- Manager's own manager: may act instead when the direct manager is away. How "away" is determined is not established (Q-001). [Customer: FEA-001 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-002]
55	- Unknown roles: whether HR or an administrator can see requests, whether a delegate role exists, and who approves a manager's own leave request are not stated. [Inferred: FEA-004 · Unknown]

101	### Submitting requests and request lifecycle

103	Employees raise leave requests that move through four statuses. What a request contains and its validation are not yet defined.

108	- **FR-002** A request has one of four statuses: pending, approved, rejected or cancelled. [Customer: FEA-007 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-004]

# Leave Requests and Manager Approval: Feature Specification

## 1. Document Status

- Run ID: 20261013-112757-565166
- Date: 2026-10-13
- Run mode: fixture
- Publication status: pending final pass
- Known limitations: The mockup capture is partial. Two of four pages failed to capture (PAGE-003 Sick leave detail and PAGE-004 New request, both HTTP 404) and three requests were blocked, so the capture inventory is incomplete. Research ran in fixture mode with no live search. One finding was kept and it has low confidence; the research questions on how HR leave systems model a temporary approver and on leave-date validation rules remain unanswered. Research was limited by DEC-005 to the first two research gaps. No existing-system documents were supplied. This draft has not yet been validated or reviewed.
- Open stale items: none
- Unresolved blocking issues: seven blocking customer questions are unanswered (Q-001, Q-002, Q-003, Q-004, Q-005, Q-007, Q-008; see section 16). REQ-001 and REQ-002 still carry the issue label Unknown.

## 2. Executive Summary

The customer wants employees to submit leave requests, managers to approve or reject them, and employees to see the status of each request. The customer has since confirmed that only an employee's direct manager may decide a request (that manager's own manager may act when the manager is away), that a reason is required when rejecting, that a rejected request can be corrected and resubmitted, that a request is pending, approved, rejected or cancelled, and that employees are emailed whenever the status changes.

The mockup shows only a request list and one pending request with Approve and Reject buttons. Its New request page and the Sick leave detail page could not be captured, so what a request contains and what a decided request looks like are not known.

Key open decisions, all awaiting the customer: how the system knows a manager is away; who sees which requests; what a leave request contains and its date rules; where the rejection reason is entered; who can cancel and when; whether decisions can be reversed; where reporting-line information comes from; and whether leave balances are in scope. Several other gaps were deferred by DEC-005 and are listed under Deferred.

## 3. Goals and Scope

### Goals

- Employees can submit leave requests. [Customer: REQ-001 · Unknown]
- Managers can approve or reject leave requests. [Customer: REQ-002 · Unknown]
- Employees can see the status of each request. [Customer: REQ-003 · Approved: DEC-003]

### In Scope

- Submitting a leave request, the request lifecycle, manager approval and rejection, employee status view and status-change emails to the employee, as stated in the requirements and decisions DEC-002, DEC-003 and DEC-004.
- Resolving the approved gaps listed in section 7 (the approvals are recorded in DEC-005). Their resolution depends on the customer answers in section 16.
- Whether leave balances are in scope is undecided (Q-010).

### Out of Scope / Rejected

No item has been rejected by a decision or excluded by the customer. Exclusions have not been inferred from what the mockup does not show.

### Deferred

Each item below was deferred by DEC-005. None is specified in this document beyond this list.

- GAP-007 Status-change emails: recipients, content and delivery failure. Deferred: DEC-005
- GAP-010 Two eligible approvers acting on the same request. Deferred: DEC-005
- GAP-011 Empty, loading, success and error states for the list and decisions. Deferred: DEC-005
- GAP-012 Traceability of who decided a request. Deferred: DEC-005
- GAP-013 Sick leave as health data: visibility, comments and retention. Deferred: DEC-005
- GAP-014 Accessibility of status text and decision feedback. Deferred: DEC-005

## 4. Users and Roles

- Employee: submits leave requests and sees the status of requests. [Customer: REQ-001 · Unknown] [Customer: REQ-003 · Approved: DEC-003]
- Direct manager: the only role allowed to approve or reject a request from their own direct reports. [Customer: FEA-001 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-002]
- Manager's own manager: may act instead when the direct manager is away. How "away" is determined is not established (Q-001). [Customer: FEA-001 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-002]
- Unknown roles: whether HR or an administrator can see requests, whether a delegate role exists, and who approves a manager's own leave request are not stated. [Inferred: FEA-004 · Unknown]
- The mockup gives no indication of the signed-in user or which role sees which screen. [Assumption: ASM-G-002]

## 5. Existing Mockup Coverage

Capture status: partial (fixture capture, 2 of 4 pages captured).

- Screen "Leave requests" lists two requests (Annual leave, 3 days, Pending; Sick leave, 1 day, Approved), each with an Open link, and a New request link. [Mockup: SCR-001 · Observed]
- Screen "Annual leave, 3 days" shows Status: Pending, Approve and Reject buttons that appear enabled, and a Back link. [Mockup: SCR-002 · Observed]
- Components: leave requests list [Mockup: SCR-003 · Observed], New request link [Mockup: SCR-004 · Observed], Approve / Reject button group [Mockup: SCR-005 · Observed], Back link [Mockup: SCR-006 · Observed].
- Flows: Open on the Annual leave request leads to its detail screen [Mockup: SCR-007 · Observed]; Back returns to the list [Mockup: SCR-010 · Observed].
- Open on the Sick leave request leads to a page that failed to capture (HTTP 404) [Mockup: SCR-008 · Observed]; New request leads to a page that failed to capture (HTTP 404) [Mockup: SCR-009 · Observed].
- Observed states: only the default state of the list and of the pending request. Rejected and Cancelled statuses, empty, loading, confirmation and error states are not shown.
- Ambiguous behaviours the mockup does not answer: who can approve or reject, whether only while Pending, reversibility, whether a reason is available on rejection, what follows Approve or Reject, who is notified, whether balances change, which requests a user sees, what other statuses exist, and the content of the New request screen.
- Capture limitations: PAGE-003 (Sick leave detail) and PAGE-004 (New request) returned HTTP 404 and are not in the inventory. Three requests on PAGE-001 (a stylesheet, a script and an image) were blocked in fixture mode, so styling or an image may be missing from what was captured.

## 6. Requirements Traceability

| REQ | Requirement | Treatment | Label | References |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| REQ-001 | Employees submit leave requests. | unresolved | Unknown | FR-001, FR-002, FR-003, AC-001, GAP-003, GAP-004, GAP-005, Q-003, Q-005, Q-006 |
| REQ-002 | Managers approve or reject leave requests. | partially addressed | Unknown | FR-004, FR-005, FR-006, BR-001, BR-002, AC-004 to AC-010, DEC-002, GAP-001, GAP-002, GAP-009, Q-001, Q-004, Q-007 |
| REQ-003 | Employees can see the status of each request. | partially addressed | Approved: DEC-003 | FR-009, FR-010, FR-011, AC-011 to AC-015, DEC-004, GAP-006, GAP-008, Q-002, Q-009 |

## 7. Gaps Identified

| GAP | Gap | Approval | Path | Priority | Status | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
